note: Opus review of the day-by-day view (S02), 5 Nov 2026. Stopped with 20 of 21 verdicts done (usage limit). Each verdict pairs with one finding in review order; check each before acting.

findings.title: The P04 lock covers only /api/daily: the detections export still serves every row on the held days
findings.problem: Change-log item 10.4 says the app withholds daily values in the G01 and G02 test windows until those tests have run. The comment at analysis.py:353-354 adds that "nobody, the builder included, sees them first". The lock is applied only by held_out_days() and p04_lock_state(), and they are called from nowhere but daily() and _daily(). detection_rows() (analysis.py:736-750) filters by year only. It feeds POST /api/export/detections.csv (app.py:128-139) and the page's export card. So one click hands out every observation row, with date_utc, platform and daynight, for Sindh and KP from 15 Sep to 31 Dec and for Punjab, Sindh and KP from 15 Mar to 30 Jun, 2012-2025. That is the full input of G02's season dates, and also G01's Terra and S-NPP day-pass counts.
findings.evidence: Flask test client. POST /api/daily {region: Sindh, day_month: [2020, 10]} returns 31 held-out days. POST /api/export/detections.csv {region: Sindh, years: [2020, 2020]} returns 200 text/csv with the header line "time_utc,date_utc,platform,instrument,version,daynight,latitude,longitude,...,province,source_id,used_in_harmonised_passes,row_kind". Only the header was read; no rows were read. grep shows held_out_days and p04_lock_state referenced only at analysis.py:372, 388, 450 and 458.
findings.fix: In detection_rows(), after the year filter, drop rows on held days: held, why = held_out_days(pd.DatetimeIndex(q['date_utc'].unique()), region, bbox, p04_lock_state()); q = q[~q['date_utc'].isin(held)]. Record `why` in the export (an extra column, or a 'held_out' entry in provenance.json). Add a test with EXPERIMENTS monkeypatched to an empty folder that checks only the boolean 'no Sindh 2020 export row falls in 15 Sep-31 Dec'. Also, state in 10.4 that monthly per-satellite columns stay visible (/api/analyze months and monthly.csv), as P04 section 0 already records. For most years those columns give G01's Oct-Nov Terra_D/SNPP_D ratio directly.

findings.title: A pass absent everywhere in Pakistan is shown as a real zero with status 'ok' or 'modelled'
findings.problem: The 'nothing_anywhere' test works per satellite-day: present = set of (platform, date). So when one of the two passes has no row anywhere in Pakistan (a partial outage or swath gap the FIRMS list does not record), the day still gets status 'ok' (status_text 'data'). The absent pass is then counted as 0 in D or N, in the satellite's value, in the month total, and in the harmonised value. That breaks the invariant that missing data is shown as unknown, never zero, and contradicts note 2 ('A zero means this satellite had data that day'). It is worst for day-pass-only areas, where H uses only the absent pass, and for modelled days, where Aqua's day pass carries about 99% of Aqua's Punjab detections (E00: Aqua_D n=86,340 vs Aqua_N n=687). latest_from() in the same module already treats one-pass VIIRS days as partial (analysis.py:254-259).
findings.evidence: Permitted days only. NOAA-20, Pakistan-wide: 2 Feb 2024 had 158 day rows (07:55-09:35 UTC) and 11 night rows; 3 Feb had 2 day rows and no night rows; 4 Feb is FIRMS-listed missing; 5 Feb had no day rows and 20 night rows (21:03-21:06); 6 Feb had 353 day rows. daily(region='Punjab', 2024, 2) gives NOAA20 on 3 Feb status 'ok' D=1 N=0, and on 5 Feb 'ok' D=0 N=5. S-NPP, 11 Feb 2012: no day-pass row anywhere (10 night rows; 10 Feb had 280 day rows, 12 Feb had 68). daily(region='Gilgit-Baltistan' or 'Islamabad Capital Territory', 2012, 2) has passes ['D'] and H = 0, status 'ok'. Aqua, 29 Oct 2003: no Aqua day-pass row anywhere in Pakistan (one of 161 such days in 2003-2011, none on the FIRMS list). daily(region='Punjab', 2003, 10) gives H = 186.6, 0.0 ('modelled') and 322.3 for 28-30 Oct. Over permitted days, S-NPP has only one pass anywhere in Pakistan on 110 of 2,046 days, and NOAA-20 on 65 of 1,116.
findings.fix: Build present_pass = set(zip(std.platform.astype(str), std.date_utc, std.daynight)) next to `present`. For every satellite, treat a day pass with no row anywhere in Pakistan as unknown. For S-NPP and NOAA-20, treat a missing night pass the same way. Leave MODIS night passes as counted, because there empty is the norm: Aqua has no night row anywhere on 3,455 of 5,377 permitted days. For such a pass, set D or N to None and give the day a status such as 'pass_missing' ('partly unknown: the day/night pass has no detection anywhere in Pakistan, an outage or a quiet pass'). Leave it out of month_total.days_used, and make H unknown when a pass it uses is missing. Reword note 2 to 'had at least one detection somewhere in Pakistan on that pass'. Add a test on NOAA-20 5 Feb 2024 in Punjab.

findings.title: The Terra row is labelled 'morning pass' but it adds the ~22:00 PKT night pass
findings.problem: DAILY_LABELS['Terra'] is 'Terra MODIS (morning pass)', but its values are D+N, the same as every other row. Note 5 says 'Terra passes in the morning; Aqua, S-NPP and NOAA-20 in the early afternoon and after midnight'. Terra also passes at about 22:00 Pakistan time, and in recent years that pass is a large share of Terra's small counts. So the label misattributes which pass the numbers came from, which is the very point the A2 clock story depends on.
findings.evidence: In daily(region='Punjab', 2024, 11), the Terra row has 11 detections, of which 4 are night-pass (N). In Feb 2020 it is 19 of 668. experiments/E00_first_run/result.json gives Punjab Terra_N n=3,164, median 17.23 UTC (about 22:14 PKT), and Terra_D median 6.0 UTC (about 11:00 PKT).
findings.fix: Either label the row 'Terra MODIS (late-morning and late-evening passes)', or show only Terra's day pass under the 'morning pass' label, with N kept in the tooltip. Make note 5 match: 'Terra passes at about 11:00 and 22:00 Pakistan time; Aqua, S-NPP and NOAA-20 at about 13:30 and 02:00.'

findings.title: The H source and the notes are fixed text that is wrong for unsupported areas, day-pass-only areas and mostly-outside boxes
findings.problem: For an area that fails the calibration support check, the H row's source still says 'modelled from Aqua (M2), monthly factor'. Note 3 says pre-2012 days are 'Aqua's daily count times this area's monthly conversion', yet no value is converted. harmonise() writes 'not supported (calibration failed support check)' for the same months. In day-pass-only areas, note 3 says 'Aqua's daily count', although only the day pass is converted. For a box mostly outside Pakistan, the response carries no share and no caveat. Meanwhile note 2 says a zero means nothing was detected 'here', but the part of the box outside Pakistan is never counted.
findings.evidence: daily(bbox=[67.5, 28.5, 68.0, 29.0], 2008, 11) has H statuses {not_supported, nothing_anywhere}, source 'modelled from Aqua (M2), monthly factor', and note 3 as quoted. daily(region='Gilgit-Baltistan', 2010, 11) has passes ['D']; note 3 says 'Aqua's daily count', and only the S-NPP note says 'day passes only'. daily(bbox=[60, 25, 62, 26], 2015, 11): check_box gives a share inside Pakistan of 0.148, yet the response keys have no share field and no note mentions it.
findings.fix: Build these strings from cal and the box check. When modelled and not cal['supported'], set source to 'not supported (calibration failed support check)' and replace note 3 with cal['reasons']. When passes == ('D',), say 'Aqua's day-pass count'. Pass check_box()'s share_inside_pakistan into the response. When it is below 0.99, add warnings()'s sentence about the part of the box outside Pakistan.

findings.title: The modelled month total sums per-day values rounded to 0.1, so it can disagree with the monthly calendar
findings.problem: Each modelled day is rounded to 0.1 before month_total adds the days (lines 505-508). The day-by-day 'Month' cell can therefore differ by one from the calendar's harmonised value for the same month. The lens asks that daily totals add up to the monthly record.
findings.evidence: Punjab 2008-02, M2: monthly H is 3477.522 and the calendar shows 3,478. The daily month_total is 3477.2 and shows 3,477. The unrounded sum of the daily values is exactly 3477.522. Azad Kashmir 2009-05: 1134.488 (shows 1,134) against 1134.7 (shows 1,135).
findings.fix: Keep the unrounded per-day modelled values for month_total and round once: round(float(sum(raw)), 1). Round each value only when it goes into h_vals. The total then equals the monthly record exactly.

findings.title: Infinite year or month gives a 500 instead of a 400; fractional values are silently truncated
findings.problem: daily() catches only TypeError and ValueError around int(year) and int(month). Python's JSON parser turns 1e400 and Infinity into float('inf'), and int(inf) raises OverflowError. That reaches the generic handler as an 'Unexpected server error'. Floats are also accepted and truncated.
findings.evidence: With the Flask test client, day_month [1e400, 1], [Infinity, 1] and [2015, -Infinity] each return 500 and log 'OverflowError: cannot convert float infinity to integer'. [2015.9, 1.7] returns 200 for 2015-01.
findings.fix: Use except (TypeError, ValueError, OverflowError). Better, require whole numbers: accept v only if isinstance(v, int) and not isinstance(v, bool), or if v is a str of digits. Otherwise raise AnalysisError('Choose a year and a month'). Add [1e400, 1] and [2015.5, 1] to the bad-input test.

findings.title: Worldview links of unlocked areas show held provinces' fire dots on held days
findings.problem: Links are dropped only for days held for the requested area. app.js justifies dropping them because a held day's 'fire dots belong to the frozen test too'. But the padded view of a neighbouring unlocked area covers a large share of Sindh or KP, with the VIIRS and MODIS fire layers switched on, on those same held days.
findings.evidence: Geometry only, for 15 Oct 2020, which is held for Sindh and KP. daily(region='Balochistan') gives a link whose view (bounds plus 0.3 degrees) is 13.3% Sindh. Punjab's view is 11.6% KP and 1.9% Sindh. Both links list the fire layers.
findings.fix: On a day held for any province, intersect the link's padded view with the held provinces, using _area_overlaps on the padded box. If they overlap, drop the fire layers from that link (keep the true-colour view) or drop the link. If this is accepted because Worldview is public, say so in 10.4 and in the app.js comment, instead of claiming the dots are withheld.

reviews.summary:
Front-end and accessibility review of the S02 day-by-day view: 6 real problems found, 2 medium and 4 low. Each was shown in a browser and has a concrete fix.

**How I checked.** I read the diff, then built a harness in the scratchpad. It uses byte-identical copies of c08/web/app.js, index.html and style.css. The API replies were recorded through the Flask test client (`app.test_client()`), and headless Chrome drove the page with a throwaway profile, deleted afterwards.
- Real data came only from Balochistan, a small Balochistan rectangle, Punjab 1–14 March 2015, and the empty locked months. Before anything was saved, code asserted that every held-out day had no value, no day/night split and no Worldview link (Punjab 15–31 March 2015, Sindh October 2020).
- The 2026 "latest" data and the experiment evidence were removed from the replies before saving.
- No server ran on 8766, and nothing in the repository was created, edited or committed.

**What passed:**
- **Request ordering:** the newest selection always won. This held when replies were released out of order, both with aborted requests and with late replies. A day reply for the old area that arrives after an area change is ignored.
- **Range ends:** Previous/Next never request a month outside 2003–2025.
- **Theme change:** the page redraws in the new colours. In both themes every colour step has text contrast of at least 5.39:1. Links are 5.26 (light) and 6.96 (dark), muted text 5.11 and 6.8, no-data cells 6.65 and 8.03.
- **Escaping:** I put HTML into the area name, labels, notes, reasons, status texts and Worldview URLs of a reply. All of it was shown as plain text; nothing was injected and no script ran. The satellite keys and status codes are not escaped, but they are fixed server values that users cannot change.
- **Table structure:** the caption names the table, and the column and row headers are exposed to screen readers.
- **Worldview links:** all of them can be reached with Tab in order, show a focus ring, and scroll into view when moving forward.
- **Narrow screens:** at 320 and 375 px the four month controls stay on one line and keep the names "Month" and "Year".
- **Offline:** the page made no requests outside the local files.

**Not counted as findings:**
- The held-out dot measures 4.43:1 on its darker stripe, but it is decorative and hidden from screen readers.
- Screen readers will read each date header as "N Month YYYY in NASA Worldview (opens in a new tab)", which is long when moving across columns.

**Other things you should know:**
- The builder edited app.js (a new `export-held` note), analysis.py and index.html during my review. The day-view code I tested is unchanged, and the line numbers below are from the current files.
- Drive C: has 1.4 GB free, below the project's 2 GB minimum.
- One issue outside my lens, for whoever reviews the P04 lock: lock item 10.4 covers daily values only. `/api/analyze` months and the monthly.csv export still contain monthly Terra_D/Terra_N and SNPP_D/SNPP_N for Sindh and KP, which are G01's inputs. Section 0 of P04 lists the calendar and chart monthly counts as already seen, but not Terra. This is older code, not part of this change. I did not open any of that data.

findings.title: Held-out cells' screen-reader text makes the whole page wider than the screen
findings.problem: Every held-out cell contains `held out` (app.js line 450). `.sr` is `position: absolute` and no ancestor is positioned, so the span's containing block is the whole page. The day table's scroller `#daily` (`.table-wrap`, line 108) is `overflow-x: auto` but `position: static`, so it cannot clip these spans. They stay at their place far to the right of the wide table and stretch the document sideways. This happens in any month whose held-out days run to the month end, whenever the table is wider than its card. While the lock stands, that means March (days 15–31) for Punjab, Sindh, KP, Pakistan and any rectangle overlapping them, and September (days 15–30) for Sindh, KP, Pakistan and overlapping rectangles, 2012–2025. On a phone the reader can then pan the page sideways into a blank strip about 670 px wide.
findings.evidence:
Headless Chrome on the exact app.js, index.html and style.css, with replies recorded from the test client.

Punjab, March 2015 (days 15–31 held), page scrollWidth vs clientWidth:
- 375 px phone: 1046 vs 375 (window.innerWidth also became 1046)
- 320 px: 1046 vs 320
- 800 px: 1046 vs 785
- 1024 px: 1054 vs 1009

Control month (Balochistan, November 2025, nothing held): scrollWidth equals clientWidth at every width. No overflow at 1280 px, where the table fits its card.

Cause, measured directly:
- The rightmost `.sr` right edge is 1046, the same as the page width.
- The span's offsetParent is BODY and it has no positioned ancestor.
- `#daily` computes to overflow-x: auto and position: static.

The full-page capture shots/phone_mar2015_as_seen.png shows the 375 px of content followed by blank space out to 1046 px.
findings.fix: Make the scroller the containing block. In style.css add `#daily { position: relative; }`, or put `position: relative` on `.table-wrap` (line 108). I injected this into the harness: scrollWidth then equals clientWidth at 375, 800 and 1024 px for Punjab March 2015, and all 85 'held out' spans remain. Apply this before adding more `.sr` text to cells (see the screen-reader finding).

findings.title: In an area that fails calibration, the key and notes give the wrong reason for blank harmonised days
findings.problem: When a rectangle fails the calibration support check, `_daily` marks every harmonised day before February 2012 that has Aqua data as `not_supported` (analysis.py line 525). The page draws these exactly like no-data days: style.css line 130 groups `d-not_supported` with `outside_record` and `provider_missing`, giving '–' on the grey no-data colour. The key then explains '–' as 'no data (outside the record, or FIRMS lists the day missing)'. That is false, because the Aqua row directly above has a count on each of those days. The notes also still say harmonised days are 'Aqua's daily count times this area's monthly conversion (M2, fitted on 2012–2017 months)' (analysis.py line 556), but no conversion was fitted. The H row's unused `source` field also says 'modelled from Aqua (M2), monthly factor' (line 534). The only correct statement on the card, 'no value: this area failed the calibration support check', is in a tooltip that appears only on mouse hover.
findings.evidence:
Rectangle 65, 27, 65.2, 27.2 (Balochistan only; /api/analyze calibration.supported = false), November 2010:
- Harmonised row: 26 cells with class d-not_supported showing '–', plus 4 '?'.
- Aqua row: numeric counts on those same 26 days.
- Key line: '– no data (outside the record, or FIRMS lists the day missing)'. The key never mentions the support check.
- Note shown: 'Harmonised days before February 2012 are Aqua's daily count times this area's monthly conversion (M2, fitted on 2012–2017 months). Only monthly values were tested; daily accuracy is untested.'
- Tooltip on hover: 'no value: this area failed the calibration support check'.
- Accessibility tree: those 26 cells are named '–'.

Only the summary card, much higher on the page, says 'No harmonised values before 2012 for this area'.
findings.fix:
Front end (renderDaily): give `not_supported` its own symbol and key line. For example, show 'n/a' in the cell, and when such cells are present add the key item 'n/a: no harmonised value, this area failed the calibration support check'. Remove `d-not_supported` from the no-data rule at style.css line 130, or keep the colour but use the new symbol.

Backend (`_daily`): when `modelled and params is None`, set the H row's `source` to 'no harmonised values before Feb 2012: calibration support check failed'. Swap the conversion note for that sentence too.

Add a test with a failing rectangle checking the note and the source.

findings.title: Days with no value have no spoken reason, and the day details need a mouse
findings.problem: S02 says missing days must say 'no data'. Only held-out cells get screen-reader text. Cells for no data, unknown ('nothing anywhere in Pakistan') and not supported expose just '–' or '?', which screen readers may read as silence or 'question'. The reason text (`D.status_text`) and the day/night pass split exist only in a mousemove tooltip (lines 468–477). No cell can receive focus and nothing reacts to focus or tap. TASK_BOARD B07 says the calendar parts (keyboard or tap tooltips) go with S02.
findings.evidence:
Accessibility tree in headless Chrome:
- Rectangle, November 2010, harmonised row: 26 cells named '–' and 4 named '?'.
- Terra row: 7 cells named '?'.
- For comparison, held-out cells in Punjab March 2015: 17 cells named 'held out'.

`document.querySelectorAll('#daily td[tabindex], #daily td a, #daily td button').length` is 0. The table's only listeners are mousemove and mouseleave.
findings.fix: Draw every no-value cell the way the held-out cell is drawn: `–no data`. Use short labels per status: 'no data' (outside_record, provider_missing), 'unknown' (nothing_anywhere), 'not supported', 'held out'. Leave the long wording in the key. To make the pass split available without a mouse, either add it as `.sr` text in `d-ok` cells (e.g. '12 detections: day 9, night 3') or add a 'Show day and night passes' toggle that adds D/N rows. Apply the page-overflow fix first. Otherwise these extra `.sr` spans widen the page in every month with no-data days at the right, such as NOAA-20 before April 2018.

findings.title: At the ends of the range, Next/Previous drop keyboard focus and still look active
findings.problem: `renderDaily` disables the button the reader has just pressed (lines 424–425), so focus falls back to the page body. The author rule `select, input, button { color: var(--ink); background: var(--surface); border: ... }` together with `button { cursor: pointer }` (style.css lines 68–69) overrides the browser's disabled look. A disabled ▶ therefore looks and points exactly like a working one, and clicking it does nothing.
findings.evidence:
- Focus on Next at November 2025, press Enter: once December 2025 renders, document.activeElement is BODY.
- Previous pressed from February 2003 to January 2003: also BODY.
- At December 2025, computed styles of the disabled Next and the enabled Previous are identical: 'rgb(11, 11, 11) | rgb(252, 252, 251) | rgb(195, 194, 183) | 1 | pointer' (look_identical: true).
findings.fix:
Keep the buttons focusable and mark them instead: replace the two `.disabled =` lines with `setAttribute("aria-disabled", String(atStart))` and `setAttribute("aria-disabled", String(atEnd))`. stepDaily already ignores moves outside 2003–2025.

Add CSS: `.daily-nav button[aria-disabled="true"] { opacity: .45; cursor: default; }`.

Alternative: if `document.activeElement` is the button about to be disabled, move focus to `#daily-month` first, and add a `button:disabled` style.

findings.title: Sticky satellite names without a sticky corner leave the wrong dates above them
findings.problem: Only the body row headers (`th[scope=row]`) are sticky. The 'Satellite' corner header and the date headers scroll. When the table is scrolled sideways (always on phones, and on Shift+Tab through the date links), headers whose columns are hidden under the sticky satellite names stay printed above those names. A reader can match the first visible column of counts to the wrong day. Shift+Tab often stops on a date link whose own column of counts is hidden under the names.
findings.evidence:
- Phone, 375 px, Balochistan November 2025, Shift+Tab from day 30 to day 21: dates 17–20 sit above 'Terra MODIS (morning pass)', 'Aqua MODIS' and the other labels, and the 'Satellite' header has scrolled off. See shots/phone_sticky_shift_tab.png, taken at 1:1.
- Shift+Tab through all 30 links: 16 stops (days 24, 23, 22, 21, 18, 17, 16, 15, 12, 11, 10, 9, 6, 5, 4, 3) left the focused link at x = 26–116 px. The labels' right edge is at 129 px, so that day's counts were covered.
findings.fix:
1. `table.daily thead th:first-child { position: sticky; left: 0; z-index: 2; background: var(--surface); }`
2. Give the label column a fixed width: `table.daily th[scope="row"] { width: 150px; min-width: 150px; max-width: 150px; }`
3. Add `scroll-padding-left: 150px` to `#daily`, so focus scrolling keeps the focused date clear of the sticky column.

Injected into the harness: 0 of 29 Shift+Tab stops landed under the labels.

findings.title: A failed day request shows the raw browser error and leaves the old month on screen
findings.problem:
loadDaily's catch prints `e.message` as-is. When the local server is not running, the reader gets the browser's 'Failed to fetch' (other browsers use other wording). run() at line 102 replaces that with instructions to restart the server.

The previous month's table also stays on screen while the selects already show the new month, and Previous/Next keep the old month's state.

A theme switch calls render() → loadDaily() (line 669 → line 151), so it re-fetches instead of redrawing. If the server is down, it raises the same error and leaves the other theme's colours in the cells.
findings.evidence:
Month changed from November to December 2025 with the reply made to fail:
- daily-msg 'Failed to fetch', styled as an error
- selects show 12/2025
- title and caption still say 'Balochistan, November 2025'
- Next enabled

Theme switched from dark to light with the server unavailable:
- daily-msg 'Failed to fetch'
- light theme active, but cells still use the dark ramp ('background:#0d366b;color:#ffffff')

With the server up, the switch re-requests /api/daily. Until the reply arrives the cells keep the old theme's colours: 'background:#cde2fb;color:#0b0b0b' on the dark page.
findings.fix:
1. In the catch: `m.textContent = e instanceof TypeError ? "The local server is not responding. Start it with: python -m c08.app" : e.message;`
2. On error, either clear `#daily` and `#daily-notes`, or set the selects back to `DAILY.month`.
3. On a theme change, redraw from the cached reply: if DAILY's region, month and model match the current request, call `renderDaily()` instead of `loadDaily()`.

reviews.summary:
Reviewed the uncommitted S02 change (day-by-day view) and the lock code the builder added to it during this review. Files as reviewed, by SHA-256 prefix: c08/analysis.py 6367bad71cff6116, c08/web/app.js 30512551fee25304, c08/app.py 98d861d6848144a8, tests/test_c08.py 6e71734fba4cb510. Item 10.4 of experiments/PROTOCOL_P04.md was also rewritten while I worked.

What holds:
- **No missing day becomes zero.** `day_status` returns held, outside the record, FIRMS-missing or unknown ("?") before any number. Nothing turns a missing day into 0.
- **Satellites are never added together.** Each row counts one satellite. The harmonised row uses S-NPP alone from Feb 2012 and Aqua alone before that.
- **The harmonised daily values follow the monthly record's rules.** Same passes, same model (M1's single factor, M2's factor for each calendar month), the same switch at Feb 2012 (January 2012 is modelled), and the same support check.
  - Daily totals minus the monthly harmonised value: 0 to 0.03 for Gilgit-Baltistan 2010-11 (day passes only), Islamabad 2008-08 and Balochistan 2010-11 and 2019-07. For Punjab 2012-01 the difference is −0.02 (M2) and 0.3 (M1). Punjab 2012-02 gives 0.0. Both models were checked.
- **Held days carry nothing.** No value, no day or night count, no month total and no Worldview link.
- **The lock catches the right areas for counts.** Provinces, "Pakistan" and any box that overlaps Sindh or KP by area are held.
  - Boxes that only touch a border are left open. That is correct for counts: province labels come from a strict point-in-polygon test (`contains_xy`), and a yes/no check found no Sindh or KP row inside such boxes.
- **The lock lifts on the right files.** It lifts only when `result.json` exists in the folders section 6.3 names, and the code now matches the rewritten 10.4 (spring lifts with G02 alone).
- **Tests.** The 7 S02 tests passed (`-B -p no:cacheprovider`; the working tree is unchanged).

Problems found (details in the findings):
1. **High.** The new `held_out_rows` number in the analysis reply, also printed on the page, lets anyone recover Terra's hidden October–November totals exactly. That breaks the Terra part of 10.4 and exposes G01's numerator for Sindh and KP.
2. **Medium.** Worldview links for open areas still show Sindh, KP and spring Punjab fire dots on held days.
3. Low items:
   - an open area's "0" or "?" depends on held rows elsewhere in Pakistan;
   - the wording for areas that use day passes only;
   - the Terra row is labelled "(morning pass)" but includes the late-evening pass;
   - the lock tests would print protected numbers if they failed;
   - the "–" key misses the failed-support case, and the reasons only appear on mouse hover;
   - the "had data that day" wording claims more than the data show.

Not a finding yet: item 10.4 cites a "P04 lock" entry in DECISIONS.md that does not exist yet. It should be written before the commit.

How the data rule was kept:
- Real-data checks used only Punjab outside 15 Mar–30 Jun, Balochistan, Gilgit-Baltistan, Islamabad and Azad Kashmir, plus years before 2012.
- The locked windows were only called to confirm they return nothing.
